description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 18:0x) from s521b's MERGE-READY report (decision 2) and docs/not-supported.md's new lines.  The s521 ruling for #139(b) (DECIDED ## s521) asked for `encoding(NAME) utf8` when the layer came through `:encoding(NAME)`; s521b could not: `%p-binmode-impl` / `%p-split-layers` (#1224) store ONE external format on the handle and nothing says whether `:utf8` or `:encoding(UTF-8)` set it, and a non-UTF-8 encoding (`:encoding(latin1)`) is applied but not reported at all -- a reported list that OMITS an applied layer, the inverse of the faking the ruling forbids.  ACCEPTED as a documented residue (not-supported.md) because the consumer that mattered (Capture::Tiny's _relayer) re-applies what the list says and the bytes agree for the latin1 case.

FIX SHAPE: record the layer SPELLING beside the external format when binmode / open applies it (`:utf8` -> utf8; `:encoding(NAME)` -> the canonical name perl reports: `encoding(utf-8-strict)` for UTF-8, `encoding(iso-8859-1)` for latin1 -- probe perl's exact text for each alias), and have get_layers read the spelling; `:pop` / `:raw` / `:bytes` clear it.  Probe vs perl: a handle after each of `:utf8`, `:encoding(UTF-8)`, `:encoding(utf8)`, `:encoding(latin1)`, `:raw`, `:bytes`, two binmodes in a row, and Capture::Tiny re-layering a `:encoding(latin1)` STDOUT (the capture must come back decoded as perl's).  Guard rows in Pl/t/io-layers-01.t; the companion one-file io/layers.t + io/crlf.t runs (crlf stays #139(a)).  LOW.
subject: `PerlIO::get_layers` (#3326, s521b) reports `:encoding(UTF-8)` as `utf8` and `:encoding(latin1)` as the base layers only -- the handle records its single EXTERNAL FORMAT, not the layer SPELLING that set it; record the spelling so the list reads `encoding(utf-8-strict) utf8` / `encoding(latin1)` as perl's (residue of the #139(b) ruling; LOW)
